ads.author: Josh Teal
ads.title: Midway Touchmaster Infinity Arcade Machine
ads.description: The Midway Touchmaster Infinity is a popular coin-operated, bar-top touchscreen arcade machine released by Midway Games around 1999–2000. Key Features and Specifications • Hardware: Powered by early PC components, featuring a 300 MHz Celeron processor, RAM, and a hard drive (often upgraded to solid-state drives today) running a 32-bit FreeBSD or custom PC-based OS. • Display: Uses a CRT monitor (available in 14-inch countertop or 19-inch upright models) paired with a curved capacitive touchscreen overlay. • Game Selection: Includes a vast library of casual mini-games, including card games (Solitaire, Poker), puzzles (Mah Jongg, Gem Slide), word games, and strategy games. • Playboy License: Midway famously secured an exclusive Playboy license for adult-themed mini-games and content, which owners can enable or disable via system/timer settings. • Operation: Can be configured for free-play or set up to accept coins and paper bill acceptors

ads.author: Alex D. Gorgone
ads.title: Pinball (1985) NES Nintendo
ads.description: No more losing your quarters, with the Nintendo Pinball (1985) for Nintendo Entertainment System (NES). This game is a true Nintendo classic that is still fun to play over 20 years after its release. The game has consistently had a high rating for the simple but challenging gameplay. It simulates the challenges of a real pinball machine. Gameplay is identical to traditional pinball. It starts off when the player triggers the conventional plunger launch at the bottom. The player then has to keep the ball in play using flippers on the bottom edges. If the ball falls through the bottom of the top screen, it will show up in the lower half. It will return to the top when knocked by a flipper. The ball will hit off various hurdles and targets along the way. The object of the game is to hit certain targets on the board for points. Pinball also has two different game types, varying speeds, and offerings for different levels of difficulty. Everyone from beginners to experts alike can enjoy playing. There is also an option for a two player game, upping the competitive factor. Fans of classic video games will love the Super Mario Bros bonus mode with Mario and Pauline. This scene was first available on Nintendo in Donkey Kong. This level can only be reached by hitting the ball into a bonus hole. A new screen is displayed where the player controls Mario, who is holding a platform. The object is to rescue Pauline by bouncing the ball off Mario's platform. Various targets must be hit to break the barrier and collect points. When the barrier below her is broken, the player has to catch Pauline on Mario's platform. The Pinball (1985) video game can be played on the Nintendo Original Entertainment System with classic controllers or joysticks. The original packaging for all NES games is 5.5 inches long by 4.1 inches wide, designed to fit in the Nintendo Entertainment System console. ads.description: Selling an original 1987 Twin Cobra arcade cabinet (Romstar/Toaplan). This is a complete, original cabinet that makes a perfect candidate for a dedicated restoration or a straightforward multicade/MAME conversion. The CRT monitor and power supply are working, but the original game board (PCB) currently needs logic-level repair to boot the game. The Details: Cabinet & Art: Solid cabinet with the original glass bezel and an original Romstar marquee in excellent, vibrant condition. The control panel overlay (CPO) shows typical arcade wear and peeling around the joysticks/buttons and will eventually need a reproduction sticker if you want a perfect look. Power Supply: The switching power supply is fully functional and recently dialed in. It is delivering a steady 5.12V to the board. CRT Monitor: The original CRT monitor is intact, receives power, and holds a raster/glow (no neck glow issues or broken glass). The Technical Issue (For Arcade Techs): The game board is currently stuck in a "watchdog reset loop." When powered on, the screen remains blank/gray and the audio outputs a continuous, rapid clicking/beeping sound. I have already cleaned the JAMMA edge connector, eliminated chip-creep by reseating all socketed ROMs, and verified the 5.12V line. The board is physically pristine with no gouges or visible corrosion, meaning a component (likely RAM or a logic chip) has failed internally. It will need to be diagnosed with a logic probe or sent to a mail-in repair specialist. Cabinet is sold as-is. It is heavy, so please bring a friend and a truck for loading. Ground floor pickup. Cash only.

ads.description: The RO-8 (often called the RO8 or RO-8a) is a classic radio-controlled (RC) two-meter thermal sailplane/glider designed by Richard Odle. Key Specifications & Details • Type: Radio-Control (RC) Sailplane / Glider • Class: 2-Meter / ~78 to 79-inch wingspan (approx. 200.7 cm) • Designer: Richard Odle (the 8th glider design in his series) • Power Plant: Unpowered (pure glider/sailplane), though many builders later retrofitted electric motor pods (e-sailplane conversions) • Design Traits: Known for a responsive, slow-flying, and gentle thermal-soaring profile, featuring a large tail volume • Construction: Traditionally built from balsa and plywood, upgrade. Plans and templates for building or restoring the RO-8 are preserved in vintage model aviation archives (such as Outer zone or Aero Fred) and occasionally sold as printed or digital templates
